blockers: The ratified scope (ZERO r1) still excludes content indexing while register r4 contracts a context engine; only the operator ratifies, so no session can build content without violating the method, and ZERO r2 has awaited ratification since 2026-10-23T14:09Z.

All capacity went into documentation and review: six handoffs, eleven ATAs, seventeen messages, three substrate ADRs and two constitution drafts, but no database, no git repository and no tested line of code; the only physical act is the pgvector installed today.

Coordination changed three times in six weeks and each change restarts the reading (72% of the measured cost is re-reading fixed context), so the marginal cost of each session goes to orientation and not to delivery.
Decisions K1-K9 of the knowledge substrate were treated as a general blocker, although bridge seg1 itself declares that the index core does not depend on them.

options.name: Close the scope first, then build
options.description: Ratify ZERO r2 and requirement-0003; write ADRs 0007-0009 of the engine; only then open the bridge and implement. Sequential and pure, but weeks without code.

options.name: Vertical slice now: segment 1 (local core) now, content layer in parallel
options.description: Authorize the already drafted bridge seg1 (inside the ratified r1 scope) and build it on the server while ZERO r2 is ratified; then segment 2 (hash, extraction, search cascade, MCP bridge).

options.name: Context engine directly, without a metadata core
options.description: Skip the provider table and the incremental index; ingest a subset of <data volume>\ into pgvector and measure the cascade. Quick demonstration, but contradicts ZERO r1 and line 1 of r4 (incremental indexing is the base).

options.name: Google Drive first (letter of the Project instruction)
options.description: Build the Drive metadata adapter before any content. In scope, but depends on ADR-0002, OAuth and credentials, and proves no component of the engine.

criteria.text: Conformity with the ratified scope and with the method (nothing enters without requirement, ADR, bridge)
Time to the first useful query answered by the database (days)
How much of register r4 is proven by measurement (lines 1-5, 10, 13)
Low risk of new drift or rework (10 = minimum risk)
Cost in tokens and sessions to the first converge (10 = cheapest)
Independence from still-open operator decisions (K1-K9, OAuth, credentials)

cost.statement: Quota used and week elapsed are not measurable from this cloud session; before the first fan-out they are read from <data volume>\persistent-memory\spend-ledger.md and the account panel and declared in the required form (quota X% used, Y% of the week, estimated cost Z USD). Prior estimate, to be confirmed: segment 1 with six Sonnet tasks of about 150 thousand tokens each and one 300 thousand token coordinator session is about 1.2 million tokens; segment 2, with embeddings and bakeoff, about 2 million. All inside the auto-approve envelope if the tasks are launched in series of three.

risks: Write through the bridge with stale content: every write to <data volume>\ is checked by hash before use (rule r-c8-1).
Citations of other models: no version or license enters a record without a primary source (rule r-c9-1).
pg_textsearch and pgvectorscale on Windows: treated as experimental; native FTS is the already ratified fallback (adjustment 1 of r4).
Scope drift: nothing of segment 2 starts before RAT-0003; if r2 is rejected, segment 1 proceeds alone and the plan is revised.
Non-commercial licenses: allowed in the pilot and marked as debt (rule r-c8-2).
